dedupe_keys.name: cisa national critical functions ncf set and definitions

description: The National Critical Functions are the functions of government and the private sector that CISA's National Risk Management Center considers so vital to the United States that their disruption would debilitate security, the economy, public health or safety. CISA published the initial set in April 2019 with partners from all 16 critical infrastructure sectors and later added definitions for each function. The set read on 2026-09-28 groups about 55 functions into four areas: connect (for example positioning, navigation and timing, wireless and satellite access network services), distribute (electricity distribution and transmission, cargo and passenger transport by air, rail, road, vessel, pipeline and mass transit), manage (hazardous materials, wastewater, emergencies, public works) and supply (water, fuels, electricity generation, food, chemicals, housing, information technology). Coverage is national (United States), without spatial data. Access is free on web pages and PDF documents, including 2020 and 2021 status updates and infographics per function; as a federal work it is public domain in the US, though the page does not say so. Caveats: it is a taxonomy and risk framework, not a dataset of assets, and the definitions change as CISA revises them. It serves as a common vocabulary for cascading failure, interdependency and resilience studies and for mapping assets to the services they provide. Related record: data-us-national-infrastructure-protection-plan is the sector-based framework the NCFs evolve from.
